4.7.draft: A partnership with Public Works Alliance's EMS Corps, the five-month emergency medical technician program for young adults facing barriers to employment, now delivered with California community colleges under instructional service agreements. The work develops the CPL procedures that articulate the training and reach its graduates, beginning with the more than 500 alumni the Chancellor has committed to reach for credit toward paramedicine, fire technology and emergency management degrees.

4.8.draft: A partnership with Futuro Health to award credit for its behavioral healthcare training, beginning with the Human Touch Healthcare program, which holds an ACE credit recommendation of three lower-division units. The project builds the crosswalk from Futuro's programs to aligned courses at five priority colleges (Merritt, City College of San Francisco, North Orange Continuing Education, Sacramento City and Contra Costa) and the faculty articulations that let its scholars receive CPL toward health and behavioral health degrees.
